defects.at: 120.9–129.28 (worst 122.6–129.28), designer head; src/shots/s27/drawn/designer.js HAIR/EAR-disc/TEMPLE/STRANDS, coordinates in the 125.0 frame
defects.what: The designer's head is off-model and uncanny. It is the largest object on screen for about 8 s. (a) The hair is one solid black hood that wraps the face like a balaclava. The source has a mass at about (500–700, 245–400) plus dozens of fine tapered locks falling across the forehead and right eye at (790–990, 310–600). (b) Hair and skin are swapped in places. Two pink skin discs crossed by black strands (the unnamed 'ear peeking' polygon at (560–612, 342–410) and TEMPLE at (640–700, 292–352)) read as zebra-striped ears or eyes where the source is black hair: at (585,380) the source is RGB 6,3,0 and the render is 216,167,145. Where the source shows cheek and jaw skin next to the headphone, the render is black: at (600,450) the source is 189,124,109 and the render is 16,7,5, and at (620,520) the source is 194,142,130. (c) Hair strands cross the brows at right angles, which makes 'X' marks at about (815–830, 355–390) and (895–915, 458–480), so the eyes read as dead or KO eyes. (d) There is no nose. The source has a clear nose at about (770–800, 505–535). (e) The face is flat peach with airbrushed blush; the source has hatched and inked shading.
defects.fix: Redraw the head, using the 125.0 frame as the key. Cut HAIR back to the upper-left mass, about (500–700, 245–400), and replace the black region x 600–650, y 420–600 with skin (skin #edc4aa, shade #dfab98) running down to the jaw line at about (660–740, 600–615). Delete the 'ear peeking' polygon and TEMPLE, and remove strands [[600,330]…], [[620,360]…] and [[660,300]…] that stripe them. Reroute strand [[790,336],[812,360],[822,392]] so it ends above y 350, and strand [[925,440],[900,470],[880,482]] so it ends at x ≥ 925, which removes the X marks. Add a nose: a bridge line from (770,470) to (790,520), a nostril tick at (780–800, 525–535), and a soft shade to its left. Replace the ~12 wide wedges with 35–50 tapered locks, 2–8 px at the root, fanning from under the cuff: over the forehead toward (800–990, 310–600) and down the left side of the face to about y 420. Add 1-px hatching on the cheek shadow side at x 640–700 and under the eyes.

defects.at: 122.0–129.28, arms under the head; designer.js FOREARM (640–968, 578–697) and HAND_R (800–955, 672–750) in 125.0 coords
defects.what: The forearm is drawn as a large bulbous pink blob that reads as a giant chin. The source shows a green jacket sleeve there, with only the hand in skin at about (800–1000, 620–700), with fingers. At (700,660) the source is dark ink and shadow (74,64,46) and the render is skin (171,131,110). At (900,700) the source is 111,68,55 and the render is 225,178,154. The render still shows the pink blob at (740–1180, 590–790).
defects.fix: Make FOREARM a jacket sleeve (D.jacket with fold inks) from x 620 to 800, ending in a cuff. Draw only the hand in skin, at (800–1000, 620–700), with 3–4 finger contours and knuckle ticks; add an ink shadow line under the hand at y≈700, x 850–950. For 128.6–129.28, key a second arm shape, or add a warp landmark, so that the sleeve extends to x≈1260 at y 600–720 and the fingers lie at (620–1000, 690–800).

defects.what: The source camera move is continuous across 129.28→129.32 (mean abs frame diff 19). The render pops (diff 30), because the end of s27 departs from the source where s28's first frame does not. (1) The owl stands fully visible and frontal, with both eyes, both cups and its feet at (1150–1290, 470–770). In the source it is turned three-quarters to the left (beak at about (1200,610), one eye at (1240,590) at 129.28; beak at (1265,580) and eye at (1300,555) at 129.0), and its body is hidden behind the designer's sleeve and the lid. The owl's 'turn' (turn=0.8–1.0) still reads as frontal. (2) The chair back is missing. The source has dark brown at x 60–200, y 600–830; the render instead extends the jacket to x=0 across y 540–940. (3) The left window is only pale bars at y 0–250. The source has wood frames at x 105–135 and 425–490 down to y≈420, a sill at y 400–420, a slatted radiator at (110–500, 420–600), and a sun shaft from the top left. (4) The mug handle is on the left; from about 129.0 it is on the right in the source (body about x 1700–1830, handle at x≈1800). There is also no paper sheet under the mug (source at about 1650–1760, 700–760). (5) The notebook is still visible at the bottom, at (1020–1650, 880–946) at 129.0–129.28, and so is the full pencil at (500–900, 900) at 129.23; the source shows neither by 129.24.
defects.fix: Draw the designer's sleeve (extended as in the previous item) after the owl from 128.8, so the owl's body below y≈640 is hidden. Keep the lid in front. Give the owl a real three-quarter-left head at turn ≥ 0.6: shift the face disc left, draw one eye near (1240,590) and the beak on the left edge, show one cup on the right, and hide the far eye. At 129.0 the eye is at (1300,555), the beak at (1265,580) and the cup at (1360–1420, 530–620). Shrink the jacket's lower-left: its left contour should run from (100,830) to (200,400) to (330,260) at 129.28. Add a chair back at (60–200, 600–830), fading in from 128.8. Extend the window frames to y 420 and add the sill and radiator, all riding the wall track. Mirror the mug (handle on the right) from 128.9. Move the notebook and pencil to their source end positions, off-frame or at the bottom-left, by 129.2. Target: the render at 129.28 should differ from s28's 129.32 frame by about the source's 19, not 30.

defects.what: (a) The wings cross-fade by globalAlpha (spread alpha = min(1, 1.5w), folded alpha = 1−w). At wings=0.4–0.8 (126.92–127.04) both sets are semi-transparent ghost blades. The source's wings are always opaque grey feathers that droop into the folded pose, and they are folded by 127.00. (b) The silhouette is a tall capsule or bowling pin, with head and body the same width. The source owl is a round chibi: a wide head, a smaller pear-shaped fluffy body, grey wing coverts at the sides, small ear tufts on top, and a heart-shaped cream facial disc with a grey V between the eyes. (c) The cups are oversized and yellow-gold (render cup median about 227,152,66); the source's are orange with a dark rim and a black band. (d) The spread wings are single flat blades; the source's have 4–5 feathered primaries. (e) The landing shadow is faint. The source's is a large soft purple-grey patch to the left, about (1100–1320, 680–780) at 126.84–127.24. (f) At 127.00 the source is a squint-wink (left eye half-closed, right eye closed); the render shows the left eye fully open. (g) During the flight out, the render owl leads the source by about 40 px (≈1 frame) at 126.24–126.28.
defects.fix: Replace the alpha cross-fade with a pose interpolation: rotate each spread wing about its shoulder into the folded position over 126.92–127.00, always at alpha 1. Rebuild the body as head width ≈1.15× body width, with a pear body and fluffy chest ticks. Add two small ear tufts and the heart-shaped disc outline with a grey V between the eyes. Scale the cups down about 20%, recolour them to about #e8883a with a #3a2a26 rim and black band. Give the spread wings 4–5 primaries. Darken and widen the landing shadow: rgba(90,70,90,0.5), 220s × 40s, centred at x−110s. Make 'wink' half-close the left eye. Shift OWL_K x at 126.20–126.28 by about +35 px.

defects.what: The render draws the edge-on lid as a thin dark slab (#3b3535), and at 128.73 as a dark narrow back panel. In the source the lid never goes dark here. At 128.48–128.52 the screen is still a narrow dark strip inside a silver frame. At 128.60–128.72 the lid is a light silver or beige aluminium edge and back, about 30–40 px wide and bright. The render reads as a black line flicking across the frame.

Keep a minimum width of about 28 px, not 14, at 128.60–128.68.

defects.what: The source's sunlit look is missing. The source has diagonal window-light shafts across the wall right of the laptop and across the desk: a bright wedge left of the laptop at 118–122 (for example about x 540–900, y 780–900 at 121.5) and bands between the laptop and notebook. It also has soft cast shadows: the laptop's pink-brown shadow off its left-front edge at (470–560, 760–810), plants and pots on the wall at (230–290, 130–190), the speakers to their left at (420–460, 430–550), and the notebook, pencil and mug on the desk. The render has one faint shaft and faint shadows. The blurred L* difference map shows red/blue banding across the desk. Mean luma is fine (±2), so this is local light, not exposure.
defects.fix: Add 2–3 soft diagonal light polygons, rgba(255,240,205,0.35–0.5) at 20–30 px blur, on the desk and on the wall near the window, riding the desk and wall homographies. Add seeded soft drop shadows, rgba(150,90,80,0.35) at 8–12 px blur, offset down-left by about 12–25 px, for the pots, speakers, laptop base, notebook, mug and pencil.

defects.what: Timing and zoom match; the correlation-fit zoom is 1.96 in both at 117.60, and 1.30 vs about 1.30 at 117.70. At 117.60, however, the wash is too white: render RGB 191,184,179 vs source 178,173,169, and the centre 209 vs 196. At 117.52–117.56 the source streaks are longer and more colour-fringed than the render's.
defects.fix: Lower the WHIP_FX wash at 117.60 from 0.62 to about 0.5 and tint it slightly grey-violet ([0.97,0.95,0.95]). Optionally raise the radial amount at 117.52–117.56 from 0.17 to about 0.22 and add a small RGB split.

defects.at: whole segment (global, src/lib/post.js; not s27's file)
defects.what: The render's grain has a regular horizontal row pattern with a period of about 5.2 px (row-mean std 1.6 vs the source's 0.9). It comes from the integer-coordinate hash in post.js, and the same pattern is visible in s28 renders. Grain amplitude is also lower than the source's paper speckle (high-pass std 2.7 vs 4.1 on the desk).
defects.fix: Report to the post.js owner: hash on (px + 0.5) with an irrational-offset 2D hash (for example a pcg or ivec-based hash) to kill the periodicity. For s27, the post grade hook (grade: { grain }) could raise grain to about 9/255.

defects.what: The snapshot renders at floor(t·30)/30 but takes the reference frame at ceil(t·25). Pairs at arbitrary times can therefore be misaligned by up to about 1.5 frames: 117.521 renders at 117.50 (s26) against source 117.56, and 126.281 renders at 126.267 against source 126.32. 117.52 itself cannot be rendered, which explains the fidelity log's 117.52 note. The film's real 25-fps frames are not affected; I checked that the GSAP clock gives exactly 117.52 and 129.32.
defects.fix: Use multiples of 0.2 s for exact pairs, or pair each render with the source frame at round(floor(t·30)/30·25), as snapshots/s27-rev1-meas/*strip*.jpg do. The tool owner could quantize the render to the composition's data-fps=25.

verdict:
"approx" is the honest rating, and nothing better. The timing, framing, camera and plane moves, and the placement of the room, laptop, props, the designer's outer silhouette and the owl's path are measured and match closely. Hold ΔE8 is about 4.8; the turn is 5–8, the owl section 8.3–8.8, and the end orbit 9.4–11.8.

- **Cuts:** the cut in at 117.52 matches the source. The pull-back zoom curve matches frame by frame (1.96/1.96 at 117.60, 1.30/1.30 at 117.70), and its luma timing matches too.
- **Owl beats on time:** it leaves the screen at about 126.34, the ^^ blink starts at 126.88, and it lands at about 126.92.
- **Designer entry:** starts at about 120.87 in both.
- **Lid:** goes edge-on at about 128.6 in both.
- **Edge overlays:** at 123.5, 125.0 and 129.28 the laptop, mug, notebook, shelves and beanie/jacket outlines sit within about 5–15 px of the source.
- **Clean output:** no red error bars, no placeholder text, and no tool errors.

**Determinism:** 118.00, 125.00, 127.00 and 129.28 were rendered in two separate compare runs (snapshots/s27-rev1-a and s27-rev1-c). The frames are bit-identical (max diff 0).

The drawing is where it falls short, and three things are highly visible:
1. **The designer's head is off-model and uncanny.** A black balaclava of hair, striped pink ear discs, X-shaped eye marks where strands cross the brows, and no nose.
2. **The forearm is a giant pink blob** where the source has a green sleeve and a small hand.
3. **The end orbit diverges from the source.** The owl stands frontal and fully visible where the source shows it turned and occluded. The chair, the window frames and radiator are missing, the mug handle is mirrored, and the notebook and pencil stay in frame. As a result there is a visible pop into s28 at 129.30, where the source is one continuous move.

Secondary gaps:
- The owl is a capsule with ghost cross-faded wings.
- The edge-on lid is drawn as a black line, where the source's is silver.
- The desk front edge is 12 px high during the hold and slides wrongly during the turn.
- The window-light shafts and cast shadows are missing.
- The beanie crown and jacket are 20–50 levels too dark.
- The pencil is thin and yellow.

The fidelity log's claim that "his shapes are placed within about 5–15 px" is true of the outlines only; the interior hair and skin regions are wrong over areas of about 100 px.

**Outputs:**
- Compare pairs: /Users/computer/rootline/apprentice-film/snapshots/s27-rev1-a (0.5 s grid), s27-rev1-b (offset grid plus boundary frames 117.48/117.50/129.32/129.36) and s27-rev1-c (exact-frame and determinism set).
- Motion: s27-rev1-motion (5 fps sheet.jpg plus sidebyside.mp4).
- Measurement crops: s27-rev1-meas. The most useful are time-true render/source strips (owl_land.jpg, owl_exit.jpg, whip.jpg, lid.jpg, entry.jpg, mug.jpg, bottom.jpg), gridded crops (gc*.jpg), edge overlays (e*.jpg), the brightness difference map (dL.jpg) and the s27→s28 boundary (boundary_end.jpg).

No source files were edited. Nothing outside snapshots/s27-rev1-* and my scratchpad was written or deleted. My own outputs were kept (about 940 MB) so they can be inspected.
